details:
This is a complicated and difficult one but I'll describe as clearly as I can with my limited knowledge on the code terminology.

Currently Pickups in Worlds are all always sending information over the Network to users in the instance to Sync their Transforms. This means that over a certain count, this Syncing process begins to lag resulting in Pickups floating behind where they actually are, sometimes by several feet.

This is unnecessary. Pickups only need to send new data on their transforms when they are actually moving.

My suggestion is to rework how the VRCPickup objects sync with users to reduce lag and allow more Pickups to exist in a world at once. They should have 2 states, 'Active' and 'Stationary'. These states should be exposed to Udon for map makers. 

When Active, Pickups send sync data over the network constantly like they currently do. 

When Stationary, pickups send sync data at an offset (so they don't all send it at once and cause hitching) randomized within a set range that can be set by the map maker (IE: Every 20-30 seconds, and it picks a value in that range), as well as every time a player joins an instance to initially set their position etc. Pickups only become Active when held by a player, or when physics calculations are still registering that it is moving. Add a 15 second buffer before toggling it to Stationary, and boom.

Pickups that are sitting on a table do not need to send updates on their position over the network in a continuous flow, they are not moving.

Some friends of mine actually got something like this working WITHIN Udon itself but due to their limitations and technically circumventing VRC's Pickup code, they couldn't get exact rotations and things to work. But it is, theoretically, possible.
title: Reprogram the VRCPickups system
